Orbs that look like the agent, and chats you can keep on screen. That is this release.

0.5.2 drew every local CLI as a mark in the corner and left the rest of the circle as two letters. Since then a project's `CLAUDE.md` can name the agent, put a face on it, and pick the voice it reads a turn in; an OpenClaw channel with two people in it is drawn as those people rather than as a room-name; a picture the gateway delivered actually shows up in the chat panel; and a panel you pin stays put instead of vanishing the moment you click away.

Still a beta. Personas were measured against real `CLAUDE.md` files on a Mac, including this repository's own. OpenClaw pictures and room orbs were measured against a live gateway. See *Known limitations*.

## New: a persona from the markdown beside the work

An orb is normally named for whatever Claude Code decided the conversation was about, falling back to the folder. **If a project's `CLAUDE.md` says what the agent working there is called, the orb wears that instead** — its name, its picture, and the voice it reads a turn out in.

Nothing is turned on and no new file is introduced. It reads the Markdown that is already beside the work, and a project that says nothing about a persona is drawn exactly as it was before.

A bullet, YAML front matter, a bold field, a table row under a persona heading, and a marked fenced block (`<!-- persona:start -->` … `<!-- persona:end -->`) all carry the same three fields. A picture path is resolved against the file that named it and against the workspace root, so a generator that writes `avatars/leota.png` next to `CLAUDE.md` and one that writes it from the project root both work. Pictures are capped at 16 MiB.

Two Claude Code sessions in the same folder no longer share one persona between them: the orb is keyed by the agent, not by `(cwd, source)`. A file at `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is not where a per-agent persona lives; `profiles/<name>/` is.

## New: an OpenClaw channel is the people in it

**An agent's picture is its orb, and a channel's orb is everyone in it.** An agent with an avatar set in OpenClaw wears it instead of its letters. A channel gets its own orb only once a second agent is in it — one agent talking in a channel is drawn as that agent, with the `#` badge. A second joining is what makes the room a thing, cut into a wedge per member, at most four, the four most recently active.

Only agents who still have an orb of their own get a wedge, so a quiet member stays in the conversation you open and drops off the faces. Heartbeat and cron sessions keep the shapes 0.4.3 gave them.

A workspace markdown file can also name a voice, a blend of Kokoro voices, and an optional speaking rate. When the gateway is on a paired peer, that already-resolved voice can travel over the peer link without sending the workspace files.

## New: pictures in the OpenClaw chat panel

A picture the gateway delivered — live, from history, from a cron, or named as a trailing path on the caption — draws as a thumbnail in the panel rather than as a path you cannot click. A refusal from the gateway says why the picture did not load, instead of looking like nothing was sent.

## New: pin a chat, and the header says where you are

**The pin in the header keeps a chat open.** A panel normally hides the moment you click anywhere else. Pin it and it stays where it is, its header becomes a title bar you can drag, and you can pin as many as you like. The next orb you click opens the ordinary come-and-go panel beside them, not on top of them. Size belongs to the agent, not the window: each one reopens at whatever you last dragged it to.

**The header says which conversation this is, and where it is happening** — the name and picture, then the session Claude Code calls this chat, the folder it is working in, and the machine it is running on. The machine is named always, and drawn in the session's own colour when it is not this machine.

A session with no terminal pane can still be reached: a delivered message is typed into Claude Code's own messaging socket rather than vanishing.

## New: a vertical line, and Grok usage that stays honest

The arrange button gains a **Vertical Line** shape, next to the ones that were already there.

Settings → Grok Build, **Keep Grok usage fresh automatically** (off by default) starts and stops Grok in the background so the weekly credit figure is not whatever Monday's session wrote. macOS only; Windows no-ops rather than guessing at a pty API this app does not wrap.

Codex usage is now asked of Codex rather than waiting for a session to write a snapshot. Usage orbs also poll as often as the number is actually changing, and they breathe through a style instead of a fire-and-forget task that could leave a ring stuck.

## Fixed

- An OpenClaw orb pinned "generating" forever by a stuck task, or by the gateway's `sessions.changed` chatter, goes idle when the work actually stopped.
- Settings no longer draws "Give each session a colour" twice.
- The chat header no longer repeats a gateway session's channel under its own chip.
- Hovering an orb no longer flickers the thought-bubble tooltip, including the account orb and the case where the tooltip overlapped the orb.
- A window that parked its conversation retires its orb. A room with one agent is not drawn as a room. A room orb no longer keeps faces for people who have gone idle.
- The default usage orb no longer inherits another account's numbers.
- OpenClaw starts its gateway connection before the screen-unlock wait, so a locked Mac mini still answers.
- Dialing an already-known peer fires the connected event, so a reconnect is not silent.
- A persona picture written as a code span, a blended voice, fenced YAML, a bold field, or a table row is actually read; a picture outside the workspace is refused rather than failing open.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.3-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.3-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.3-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.5.3-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the right one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or `Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.5.2-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged, so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Local Network permission does not.** Replacing the app loses the grant, and paired machines plus an OpenClaw gateway start failing with `No route to host`. Approve it again in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network. A headless Mac still cannot; pair from the machine with a screen and add the headless one by address.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and leaves your hook configuration alone.

Personas are on as soon as a `CLAUDE.md` names one; there is no new switch. Grok auto-refresh is off by default.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click **Install Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave the hook checkboxes ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"** too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code, Codex, and Grok each run. Until it's wired in, the app starts and runs correctly and shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them. Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than duplicating.

## Known limitations

Everything below is named because it was not measured, not because it is expected to fail.

- **Windows personas, Windows OpenClaw pictures, and Windows Grok auto-refresh have not been run** against a live CLI on that OS. CI runs the parse and UI tests on both legs. Grok auto-refresh is a documented no-op on Windows.
- **Grok usage is as fresh as the last Grok session's log line**, unless auto-refresh is on — and auto-refresh is macOS only.
- **Codex usage is as fresh as Codex will answer**, or as the last rollout `token_count` if it will not.
- **Local Network consent is lost on every upgrade**, same as 0.5.2.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info → Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.
